answer: A museum hires agent-run foundries to turn each vertex of a fable's plot graph into a tactile plaque. The forge signs a meter reading and mold serial for each cast; a blind curator checks a random sample, and the marketplace retires the serial after one payment. Opening more agent accounts cannot redeem the same cast twice. To collect more, an attacker must buy metal and machine time for distinct plaques and risk losing a bond on failed inspections. Compromised forge keys or colluding curators can still fake casts, so independent inventory audits and appeals are needed.
